Subject: Follow up from today's call — load shape and deployment questions

Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo today — the team liked the latency numbers on the hosted path. We want to make sure we're evaluating the right deployment mode: hosted for rapid rollout vs. dedicated for predictable throughput and privacy.

To help with sizing: our short answers from the product side:
- Peak TPS (in a busy hour): ~320 TPS for text generation endpoints (chat + completion mix).
- Typical request token shape: 70 tokens prompt average, 900 tokens generation average (we're experimenting with longer responses).
- Concurrency: we expect up to ~40 concurrent inference sessions during peak.
- Embeddings workload: ~2k reqs/hr (L4-sized small model).

Procurement copied on this thread so we can start to surface any contractual questions early. Can you send a strawman capacity recommendation and any obvious blockers for a VPC/private deployment?

Best,
Elena

Subject: INTERNAL: MindMesh strawman sizing (please review)

Team — drafting a quick strawman for MindMesh based on Elena's numbers below. Please add gaps, corrections, and a conservative/optimistic column. Attaching a one-tab workbook (mindmesh-strawman_sizing.xlsx).

Summary of inputs from customer:
- Peak generation TPS: 320 TPS (hourly busy period)
- Token profile: prompt P50 ~70 tokens, generation P50 ~900 tokens; tail to 8k per request for experiments
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~40
- Embeddings: 2k reqs/hr (low priority)
- Latency target: prefer P95 <= 200ms for interactive chat; 500ms acceptable for longer completions

Strawman approach (high-level):
- GPU family options:
  * H100 (80GB): target for high-throughput, low-latency bursts; good for long-context models and large batch kernels. Expect ~110-140 gen TPS/GPU at our standard continuous-batch config for ~1k token outputs (depends on quantization).
  * A100 (40/80GB): mid tier — stable across longer sequences; ~70-100 gen TPS/GPU for 1k token outputs.
  * L4 / T4x: inexpensive for embeddings and smaller rerank models; not ideal for long-gen at scale.

- Sizing quick math (conservative): assume 320 TPS / 100 TPS per H100 ~ 4 H100s baseline; plan for 2x headroom for peak bursts and failover => 8 H100s reserved.
- Concurrency knobs: target 10-12 model instances per GPU with continuous batching window tuned to 20–40 ms for interactive SLOs.
- Token mix impact: average 970 tokens/request => larger batching and KV cache benefits. Recommend prefix KV caching for repeated prompts (30–40% hit expected).
- Autoscale policy: maintain reserved pool (dedicated) at commit for baseline; allow burst capacity from shared infra for unpredictable spikes.
- Networking/IO: ensure 100 Gbps NICs for H100 nodes in VPC; pre-warm cache population during scheduled ramping windows.

Open questions for Elena to confirm before we finalize:
1) Can they share P50/P95 token lengths (or examples) for the "long response" experiments?
2) Any data residency constraints beyond US region?
3) What is their tolerance for quantized model fidelity? Are we allowed to recommend int8 quantized variants for cost savings?

Deliverables: I'll turn this into a one-page recommendation for Elena, include expected monthly committed GPU hours and an ops checklist for VPC. Please flag any technical redlines.

Sofia

Quick notes inline — overall the H100 baseline looks reasonable. A few adjustments + ops notes: 

- TPS per GPU callouts: the 110-140 TPS estimate for H100 assumes aggressive kernel selection + BF16/FP16. If they insist on strict fp32 fidelity we'll hit ~60-70 TPS. Recommend we show two rows (perf vs fidelity).
- Concurrency: if they have long-lived sessions (websocket chat) we should account for holding KV cache slots; reduce instance density to 6–8 per GPU when average response >2k tokens.
- KV cache hit: 30–40% is optimistic for brand-new prompts — but for product use-cases with repeated templates the 30% is fair. Recommend we model 0%, 25%, 40% scenarios in workbook.
- Autoscaling: Reserve committed pool (8 H100s) + configured burst to N+2 H100 on demand. Include a fallback to a slightly cheaper A100 pool when H100 scarce.
- Networking: concur on 100 Gbps for cross-node KV transfers; also call out egress cost for model artifacts sync in VPC bootstrap.

Ops checklist to include in the deliverable: secure KMS integration, audit-level logging (token-level tracing off by default), pre-signed access for container images, and a runbook for model rollback (canary + instant fallback to hosted).

I'll tweak the workbook with the perf/fidelity rows and a 3-scenario cost tab.

—Karthik
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

Elena — attaching a concise strawman and an ops checklist (see attached workbook). High level summary for your leadership and procurement: 

Recommendation (short):
- Baseline committed pool: 8x H100 (80GB) nodes. Rationale: provides predictable baseline throughput (conservative 320 TPS target) and headroom for bursts when combined with autoscale.
- Perf vs fidelity options: provide two SKU paths in the workbook: H100 (high perf / bf16) and A100 (mid perf / fp32-friendly).
- Concurrency: plan for 6–12 model instances/GPU depending on average output length (we modeled both).
- Token mix assumptions used: P50 request total tokens = 970; tail up to 8k. We included scenarios with lower/higher averages.
- KV cache assumptions: modeled 0/25/40% hit rates — recommend instrumenting early to capture real hit rate and tune cache size.

Operational asks for VPC/private deployment:
- KMS credentials and IP allowlist for VPC peering engineers.
- Time window to pre-warm models (recommended 2–3 hours before planned traffic ramps).
- Confirmation on quantization tolerance (we propose int8 for cost-savings in non-critical flows).

Next steps:
1) Review attached workbook with your engineering team (mindmesh-strawman_sizing.xlsx).
2) If the baseline looks good, schedule a 60-min deep dive with Karthik and Marissa to validate kernel/perf tradeoffs and finalize committed hours (link: https://app.hubspot.com/meetings/sofia/checkout?deal=DEAL-9934).
3) Procurement: we'll follow up with a contract addendum for reserved capacity and an ops checklist for VPC onboarding.

If helpful, we can also run a short 24–48 hour pilot on a small dedicated pool to capture real token shape and KV-hit metrics before final commit.

Thanks — looking forward to the next meeting.
